messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up — after merging the new attention kernels CI started failing during fatbin linking. Local builds on my workstation are fine; CI shows mixed PTX headers across matrix nodes so the linker bails.

Dylan: Hit this too. Error is `cuobjdump: incompatible ptx version in fatbin` on ubuntu-18 and mac runners. :grimacing: CI log attached.

build-bot: [CI] build/runtime-kernels #842 failed on eng-runtime-linux-ubuntu18 (linker): exit code 1

maya: Root cause analysis so far: our matrix includes builders with CUDA 11.x defaulting to PTX 6.x and CUDA 12.x producing PTX 7.x. We currently emit a PTX fallback via `-gencode=compute_X,code=compute_X`, and nvcc chooses the PTX version based on the toolkit. That leads to inconsistent PTX blobs inside fatbins.

alex: Two immediate approaches: 1) Normalize nvcc invocation across the matrix by forcing explicit ptx/code targets where supported; 2) Post-process CI artifacts to normalize PTX headers before fatbin packaging (rewrite header or strip PTX). The latter is a bit gnarly.

srini: Rewriting PTX in CI is brittle. Alternative: stop producing fatbins for these kernels — produce per-arch cubin+ptx pairs and upload a split archive (no single fatbin). Runtime can pick the matching cubin or ptx at load time.

nora: Split artifacts will help compatibility but will affect the size gate. Splitting increases total repo size though per-file size drops. Suggest updating `artifact-size-gate` to measure compressed archive size instead of raw fatbin bytes.

maya: Proposal we can act on today:
- Build produces `kernel-smXX.cubin` and `kernel-smXX.ptx` per SM target (no fatbin).
- CI uploads a single index JSON listing available artifacts and their sm targets.
- Add a CI linter job that runs `cuobjdump --dump-elf` and `cuobjdump --ptxinfo` on linux runners to validate the toolchain matrix.

Dylan: Example nvcc invocation that produced consistent PTX on CUDA12 hosts in my tests:
```
nvcc -arch=sm_90 -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=sm_90 \\
     -gencode=arch=compute_90,code=compute_90 \\
     -Xptxas -v -O3 -o kernel.o kernel.cu
```
Note: if you omit the `compute_90` fallback the toolchain may not emit PTX for older hosts.

alex: Also look at `-Xfatbin --compress-all` to reduce artifact size. Some nvcc versions support it; guard with a feature probe in CI so we fallback if not present.

ops-ci: Mac builders don't ship `cuobjdump`. We should run the PTX verification only on linux verifier images. I'll provision a small verifier image (container) with nvcc and cuobjdump and schedule those jobs on linux-only runners.

srini: Runtime-side compatibility: add a loader shim that prefers cubin if PTX header mismatch is detected. That keeps older nodes running and lets newer nodes use PTX for forward compatibility. I'll draft a tiny patch.

maya: Action items:
- alex: add `--compress-all` probe and safe fallback in CI (linux) — due EOD.
- dylan: add split-artifact build script and JSON index format; open PR by tomorrow.
- ops-ci: publish verifier container image with `nvcc` + `cuobjdump` and route linter jobs to it.
- srini: update runtime loader to prefer cubin on PTX mismatch (small patch).
- dylan: update `ci/size-gate` to measure compressed tarball size and set a +6% regression threshold for compressed artifacts only.

nora: Perf/regression tests will need a new baseline because kernels are now split; mark these regressions as non-blocking for the initial rollout.

maya: I'll add notes to the RFC follow-up doc and link the PRs. If anyone hits reproducible failures, paste the failing `cuobjdump` output here.

alex: Debug tip — if a fatbin links but a runtime node hits illegal instruction, run `cuobjdump --dump-resource` and compare SM IDs between cubin and target device. That saved me earlier today. :coffee:

build-bot: [CI] queued: kernel-split-build on eng-runtime-linux-ubuntu22
